'''Kosta Perović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Коста Перовић}}; born February 19, 1985) is a Serbian former professional [[basketball]] player. He represented the [[Serbia national basketball team|Serbian national basketball team]] internationally. In the [[2006 NBA draft]] he was a second-round selection of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Golden State Warriors]], with whom he signed on August 3, 2007. A {{convert|2.17|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} [[Center (basketball)|center]], Perović was the tallest player taken in the 2006 NBA Draft. His game has been compared to that of Slovenian center [[Radoslav Nesterović]].<ref>[http://www.draftexpress.com/viewprofile.php?p=147 DraftExpress NBA Draft Prospect Profile: Kosta Perovic, Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook.<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060614151956/http://www.draftexpress.com/viewprofile.php?p=147 |date=2006-06-14 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Europe===
Perović was born in [[Osijek]], [[Socialist Republic of Croatia|SR Croatia]], in the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|former Yugoslavia]]. He played basketball professionally for [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] at the time of his being drafted by the [[Golden State Warriors]].

After being drafted in 2006, Perović did not immediately come to the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. Rather, he played the 2006–07 season in the [[Naša Sinalko Liga|Serbian League]].

===NBA===
On August 3, 2007, Perović was signed to a two-year contract worth about US$3.5 million with a team option for a third season by Golden State. On November 18, 2007, he was assigned to the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]] after going without an appearance in Golden State's first seven games. He played for the Warriors' affiliate team, the [[Bakersfield Jam]] until January 6, 2008, when he was recalled to the Warriors' squad after they waived [[D. J. Mbenga]].

Perović played his first minutes in an [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] game with the Warriors on January 19, 2008, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], in which he scored 4 points (on 2 of 2 field goal shooting) and 4 grabbed rebounds (2 offensive), as well as blocking a shot.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=280119015 Warriors 119, Bucks 99.]</ref> In 7 games in the NBA, he averaged 1.4 points and 1.9 rebounds per game.

===Spanish teams===
After being waived by the [[Golden State Warriors|Warriors]] on September 12, 2008,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_waive_perovic.html Warriors Waive Kosta Perovic.]</ref><ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/coid_rL8os2LbGg2AVSOZwIoqP0.articleMode_on.container_frontpage.html Serbia's Perovic Waived by Warriors.]</ref> Perović reportedly signed a three-year deal worth [[Euro|€]]3.3 million [[net income]] with  [[Valencia BC|Pamesa Valencia]] of the Spanish [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]].<ref>[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/54330/20080909/kosta_perovic_signs_with_spanish_club/ Kosta Perovic Signs With Spanish Club.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080911215910/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/54330/20080909/kosta_perovic_signs_with_spanish_club/ |date=2008-09-11 }}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080924005209/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/34937/448 Pamesa signs center Kosta Perovic]</ref> After a mutual termination of the contract with Pamesa Valencia in June 2010, Perović signed with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet]].<ref>[https://thehoopsmarket.blogspot.com/2010/06/regal-barcelona-signs-kosta-perovic.html Regal Barcelona signs Kosta Perovic]</ref> In the 2009–2010 season, he averaged 8.4 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.

On August 19, 2012, he signed a one-year deal with the [[ACB League|Spanish]] club [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Unicaja Malaga adds size with Kosta Perovic|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/42666/unicaja-malaga-adds-size-with-kosta-perovic.html|work=Sportando|access-date=19 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Moutis|first=Lefteris|title=Unicaja's powerful front line|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/2012/08/dribbling/8512|work=eurohoops.net|access-date=19 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120824224233/http://www.eurohoops.net/2012/08/dribbling/8512|archive-date=24 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Unicaja Malaga waives Krunoslav Simon and Kosta Perovic|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/56034/unicaja-malaga-waives-krunoslav-simon-and-kosta-perovic.html|work=Sportando|access-date=2 July 2013}}</ref>

===Russia===
In August 2013, Perović signed a one-year deal with [[BC Yenisey Krasnoyarsk|Yenisey Krasnoyarsk]] of Russia.<ref>{{cite web|script-title=ru:Коста Перович и Александр Павлов|url=http://www.basket-enisey.ru/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=2976:2013-08-12-05-18-31&catid=44:2008-09-02-05-42-59&Itemid=125|access-date=12 August 2013|language=ru}}</ref> In July 2014, he extended his contract with Yenisey for one more season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kosta Perovic remains with Enisey Krasnoyarsk|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/128500/kosta-perovic-remains-with-enisey-krasnoyarsk.html|access-date=22 July 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref> In December 2014, he got injured and missed the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Enisey Krasnoyarsk big man Kosta Perovic reportedly done for season|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/144864/enisey-krasnoyarsk-big-man-kosta-perovic-reportedly-done-for-season.html|access-date=25 December 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref>

===Return to Partizan and retirement===
On September 29, 2015, he returned to Partizan Belgrade.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kosta Perović, Aleksandar Cvetković i Andrej Magdevski ponovo zadužili crno-belu opremu|url=http://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/1679/kosta-perovic-aleksandar-cvetkovic-i-andrej-magdevski-ponovo-zaduzili-crno-belu-opremu|access-date=30 September 2015|work=kkpartizan.rs|date=29 September 2015|language=sr}}</ref> Struggling to return to his previous form after few months of absence due to a knee injury, he retired from professional basketball on December 15, 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kosta Perović okončao karijeru|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=12&dd=15&nav_id=1074976|access-date=15 December 2015|work=b92.net|date=15 December 2015|language=sr}}</ref> He appeared in 12 games of the [[2015–16 ABA League|ABA League]], averaging 3.1 points and 2.1 rebounds per game.

==National team career==
Perović played for the [[Serbia men's national under-16 basketball team|FR Yugoslavian U16 national team]] at the [[2001 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship|2001 European Championship]] and won a gold medal.
He began his senior national team career at the [[EuroBasket 2003]] when Serbia and Montenegro finished with 6th place. Perović has also been a member of the senior men's [[Serbian national basketball team]]. With them he won the silver medal at the [[EuroBasket 2009]]. In the following year, he was member of team that finished 4th at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship|World Championship]] in Turkey. At the [[EuroBasket 2011]] in Lithuania, where he was capped, Serbia finished 8th.

== Post-playing career ==
Perović owns and operates a [[cherry]] orchard and a plantation of organic ethereal herbs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Intervju, Uroš Tripković: Od "bloka za Uroša" do plantaža borovnica |url=https://moravainfo.rs/2019/01/intervju-uros-tripkovic-od-bloka-za-urosa-do-plantaza-borovnica/ |website=moravainfo.rs |access-date=5 March 2019 |language=sr |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306043853/https://moravainfo.rs/2019/01/intervju-uros-tripkovic-od-bloka-za-urosa-do-plantaza-borovnica/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
